subject: fix(provider): keep the account boundary honest at its edges
instruction:
fix(provider): keep the account boundary honest at its edges

The Codex account connection queued requests behind a slow initialize
with no caller-liveness check, so a caller whose ceiling expired still
had its request dispatched upstream — a real logout nobody was waiting
for — and was answered into a corpse. flush now skips queued entries
whose caller has exited and keeps draining; the surviving request is
proven to be the only one on the wire, under its own id.

A response carrying a non-integer id could never match anything here,
and fell through silently: the caller burned its whole timeout learning
nothing. Such frames are named in a warning now.

Also, three smaller edges the review turned up:

- capability module names are bounded to eight dotted segments before
  Module.concat interns them; the atom table has no collector;
- the cache-policy watchdog sleeps whole POSIX seconds instead of
  relying on GNU/BSD float extensions of /bin/sleep;
- DataDir creates its own missing parent components at 0700 rather
  than under the ambient umask, while leaving pre-existing parents
  exactly as their owner made them.

HarnessEventProjection's moduledoc now states which lane carries
provider-env secret redaction and what callers projecting events from
outside that lane owe.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - a request whose caller exits while initialization is pending is dropped, not dispatched

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place. Work only inside this worktree.
